note: Design DNA for the Claude + Codex agent prompt (idea_wheel.build_agent_prompt). Seeded per idea id + remix index. 'blocks' = context tags that rule an item out; 'only' = item allowed only when the idea has one of these tags; 'fits' = tags that make it a strong match (used for the WHY line). Context tags come from idea_wheel.dna_context(): calm, sensitive, transactional, b2b_quote, b2b, b2c, tool, showcase, p:<pattern>, s:<sector>, st:<style>. Rule: hijack=true mechanics must block transactional, calm and b2b_quote; heavy=true must block calm; subtle=false must block b2b_quote.

contexts.calm: a calm, trust-first audience (care, health or vulnerable clients), so motion stays gentle and accessibility comes first
contexts.sensitive: a sensitive niche where clarity beats spectacle
contexts.transactional: a booking / quote / checkout flow, so the form must live in normal native scroll
contexts.b2b_quote: a B2B quote-style tool: standard scroll plus one tasteful moment
contexts.b2b: business buyers who scan before they read
contexts.b2c: consumers deciding in the first few seconds
contexts.tool: an app-like deliverable, so the mechanic lives on the concept's landing page and the tool screens stay standard
contexts.showcase: a marketing-led deliverable where the landing page is the product

mechanics.label: Sticky stacking cards
mechanics.how: Feature cards pin one after another and stack like a deck as the visitor scrolls; each new card slides over the last, which scales down slightly.
mechanics.implementation: Each card is `position: sticky` with an incremental `top` (`calc(80px + var(--i) * 14px)`); the scale-down is a CSS scroll-driven animation (`animation-timeline: view()`, `animation-range: exit 0% exit 60%`) behind `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`. Without support the cards simply stack statically. Zero JS.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Drop the scale animation and the sticky offsets; cards render as a normal spaced list.
mechanics.perf: Animate transform and opacity only; at most 6 cards; never animate box-shadow; no JS.
mechanics.mobile: Keep sticky with 8px offset steps; below 380px wide render a plain list.
mechanics.use: Stack one card per feature of the {pattern_lower} flow, starting with {feature1}, so the offer reads like a deck the visitor flips through.
mechanics.why: Native scroll stays untouched, so it is safe next to forms and booking.

mechanics.label: Clip-path reveals
mechanics.how: Screenshots and UI panels open from a soft inset or circular mask as they enter the viewport.
mechanics.implementation: `clip-path: inset(12% 12% round 24px)` animating to `inset(0)` on `animation-timeline: view()` with `animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%`; fallback: one IntersectionObserver adds `.is-in` once (one-shot, then unobserve).
mechanics.reducedMotion: No mask animation; content is fully visible on load.
mechanics.perf: clip-path on at most 8 elements per page; images carry width/height attributes so nothing shifts layout.
mechanics.mobile: Same effect with a shorter range (`entry 0% entry 80%`) so reveals finish before the thumb stops.
mechanics.use: Open each screen of the {pattern_lower} flow through a mask as it arrives, so the page feels composed without moving the scroll.
mechanics.why: A quiet, editorial motion that adds polish without competing with the copy.

mechanics.label: Scrollytelling split
mechanics.how: A sticky visual (device mockup or diagram) holds on one side while short text steps scroll past on the other; the visual swaps state at each step.
mechanics.implementation: Two-column grid; the visual column is `position: sticky; top: 15vh`; every text step is watched by one IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.6) that sets `data-step` on the visual; states cross-fade in CSS. No scroll math, no library.
mechanics.reducedMotion: No cross-fade: states switch instantly, or each step shows its own static screenshot inline.
mechanics.perf: One observer for all steps; swap pre-rendered states instead of re-rendering heavy DOM; at most 5 steps.
mechanics.mobile: Below 768px collapse to one column: each text step followed by its own static screenshot; no sticky visual.
mechanics.use: Hold a phone mockup of the {pattern_lower} screen still while the steps scroll: {step1}, then {step2}, then {step3}.
mechanics.why: Explains a multi-step flow in order while leaving native scroll alone.

mechanics.label: Scroll-linked route / timeline line
mechanics.how: An SVG line draws itself down the page (or across a simple map) as the visitor scrolls, connecting each stage of a sample job.
mechanics.implementation: SVG path with `pathLength="1"`, `stroke-dasharray: 1` and `stroke-dashoffset` animated on `animation-timeline: view()` for the section; fallback: IntersectionObserver per stage toggles pre-drawn segments.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Line fully drawn on load; stage markers static.
mechanics.perf: One path under 300 nodes; no SVG filters on the path; animate stroke-dashoffset only.
mechanics.mobile: Vertical line down the left edge with the stages stacked beside it.
mechanics.use: Draw one line through the stages of a sample job ({step1}, {step2}, {step3}) so the visitor sees the whole path from inquiry to done.
mechanics.why: The page literally follows the job, which is the story this concept tells.

mechanics.label: Step-by-step scroll rail
mechanics.how: Each section is one step of the flow; a sticky progress rail fills as the visitor reaches each step, with gentle proximity snapping.
mechanics.implementation: `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` on the step container (never `mandatory`); steps use `scroll-snap-align: start`; rail fill is a `scaleY` on `animation-timeline: scroll(nearest)`; fallback: IntersectionObserver sets the active step.
mechanics.reducedMotion: `scroll-snap-type: none` and no rail animation; the active step is still highlighted.
mechanics.perf: The rail is one transformed element; no per-frame JS.
mechanics.mobile: Rail becomes a thin top progress bar; snapping off below 768px.
mechanics.use: Give {step1}, {step2} and {step3} one section each, with a rail that shows how far through the {pattern_lower} the visitor is.
mechanics.why: Mirrors how the real flow works, so the landing page doubles as a walkthrough.

mechanics.label: Section spine + live table of contents
mechanics.how: A slim sticky spine lists the page sections and highlights the one in view; tapping a label jumps there.
mechanics.implementation: Sticky `<nav aria-label="On this page">`; one IntersectionObserver sets `aria-current="true"` on the active link; the progress fill uses `animation-timeline: scroll(root)`.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Instant jumps (`scroll-behavior: auto`) and no fill animation.
mechanics.mobile: Collapses to a horizontally scrollable chip row under the header.
mechanics.use: Spine sections: the problem, the {pattern_lower} flow, the signature moment ({signature}), the owner view, and the disclosure.
mechanics.why: Orientation for careful readers; the calmest mechanic in the catalog.

mechanics.label: Section tone shift
mechanics.how: The page background and ink tokens ease from one palette tone to the next as each section takes over.
mechanics.implementation: Register `--bg` and `--ink` with `@property` (`syntax: '<color>'`) and animate them per section on `animation-timeline: view()`; fallback: IntersectionObserver swaps a `data-tone` attribute with a 300ms transition.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Tones switch per section with no transition.
mechanics.perf: Only custom-property colour animation on one wrapper; every tone pair checked for WCAG AA.
mechanics.use: Move from the palette's base tone (the problem) to its accent (the {pattern_lower} answer) to a warm close (the CTA).
mechanics.why: Signals the shift from problem to solution without moving anything.

mechanics.label: Before / after scrub
mechanics.how: A split frame where scroll (or a drag handle) wipes from the old way (texts, notes, calls) to the new flow.
mechanics.implementation: Two stacked layers; the top layer's `clip-path: inset(0 var(--cut) 0 0)` is driven by `animation-timeline: view()`; a real `<input type="range">` drives the same custom property for keyboard and touch.
mechanics.reducedMotion: No scroll-driven wipe: both states side by side; the range input still works.
mechanics.perf: Two pre-sized images or two static DOM layers; clip-path only.
mechanics.mobile: Before stacked above after; range control full width.
mechanics.use: Before: {a_niche} running on texts and memory. After: the {pattern_lower} screen. Same frame, one wipe.
mechanics.why: Shows the change instead of claiming it, so no numbers are needed.

mechanics.label: Bento assemble
mechanics.how: Bento tiles rise and settle into place in a short stagger as the grid enters view.
mechanics.implementation: Each tile gets its own `animation-range` offset by `--i` on `animation-timeline: view()`; fallback: one IntersectionObserver adds `.is-in` with `transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms)`.
mechanics.perf: At most 9 tiles; translate up to 24px plus opacity; no blur filters.
mechanics.mobile: Single column with the stagger cut to 20ms.
mechanics.use: One tile per feature ({feature1} first and largest), each a small live widget on sample data.
mechanics.why: Feature-dense concepts read faster as a grid than as a long list.

mechanics.label: Masked hero zoom-out
mechanics.how: The hero opens on a tight crop of the product UI inside a mask that widens to full-bleed as the visitor scrolls the first screen.
mechanics.implementation: Hero wrapper `clip-path` plus inner `scale` on `animation-timeline: view()` (`animation-range: exit 0% exit 100%`). No pinning: the section scrolls normally.
mechanics.perf: One AVIF/WebP image under 250 KB or a live DOM screen; `will-change: transform` only while the range is active.
mechanics.mobile: Shorter range and a wider starting crop so the UI stays legible.
mechanics.use: Start on the signature moment ({signature}) up close, then pull back to the full {pattern_lower} screen.
mechanics.why: A cinematic first impression that still leaves scrolling native.

mechanics.label: Layered parallax depth
mechanics.how: Three or four layers (backdrop, UI cards, labels) drift at different speeds to give the hero real depth.
mechanics.implementation: Per-layer `translateY` on `animation-timeline: scroll(root)` with different ranges; fallback: static layers (no JS parallax, no scroll listeners).
mechanics.reducedMotion: All layers static at their resting positions; the hero still reads as one composed image.
mechanics.perf: At most 4 layers, transform only, never `background-attachment: fixed`; test on a mid-range phone.
mechanics.use: Backdrop: the {niche_lower} setting; middle: floating cards from the {pattern_lower} flow; front: one CTA chip.
mechanics.why: Depth makes a consumer landing page feel crafted in the first second.

mechanics.label: Kinetic type scrub
mechanics.how: The headline's weight, width or letter spacing shifts as the visitor scrolls and settles by the end of the hero.
mechanics.implementation: Variable-font axes (`font-variation-settings` or `font-weight`) animated on `animation-timeline: view()`; fallback: the settled headline.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Headline renders in its settled state.
mechanics.perf: One subset variable font (woff2 under 60 KB); animate one element only.
mechanics.mobile: Halve the axis range; text must never overflow its line.
mechanics.use: Set the hook as the headline and let its weight resolve as the {pattern_lower} screen slides in beneath it.
mechanics.why: Type does the work, so the motion costs almost nothing.

mechanics.label: Horizontal rail
mechanics.how: Vertical scrolling moves a horizontal track of panels sideways while the section stays pinned.
mechanics.implementation: Section height = panels x 100vh; an inner `position: sticky` viewport; the track's `translateX` runs on `animation-timeline: view()`. GSAP ScrollTrigger only if per-panel snapping is truly required (justify it in CONTRACT.md).
mechanics.reducedMotion: A native horizontal scroll container (`overflow-x: auto` + scroll-snap) with a visible scrollbar and arrow buttons.
mechanics.perf: At most 6 panels; lazy-load panel images; transform only.
mechanics.mobile: Replace with a native swipe carousel (snap inside the carousel only, never the page).
mechanics.use: Line up the concept's screens as panels so the visitor walks through the {format_lower} like a gallery wall.
mechanics.why: Turns a set of screens into a walk-through exhibit.

mechanics.label: Pinned scene scrub
mechanics.how: One scene pins while scroll progress scrubs it through states, e.g. an empty day filling up with sample records.
mechanics.implementation: Wrapper `height: 300vh`, scene `position: sticky; top: 0`; states keyed to `animation-timeline: view()` progress through CSS custom properties. GSAP ScrollTrigger (scrub) only for a canvas image sequence.
mechanics.reducedMotion: No pin: three static frames of the scene in sequence.
mechanics.perf: Scene under 1 MB total; an image sequence is at most 60 WebP frames; no layout properties per frame.
mechanics.mobile: Pin for 200vh at most, or the three static frames below 768px.
mechanics.use: Pin the owner view and scrub it from an empty day to a full one using the sample records.
mechanics.why: The scroll itself becomes the demo of the product working.

mechanics.label: Scroll-driven 3D object
mechanics.how: A 3D object (device, storefront or product) rotates and opens as the visitor scrolls past.
mechanics.implementation: Prefer CSS 3D (`transform-style: preserve-3d`, layered SVG/PNG faces) on `animation-timeline: view()`. Three.js or model-viewer only if a real model is needed, justified in CONTRACT.md.
mechanics.reducedMotion: One static render of the object at its best angle.
mechanics.perf: CSS 3D: at most 6 faces. WebGL: model under 500 KB, lazy-loaded after first paint, paused off-screen.
mechanics.use: Rotate a device showing the {pattern_lower} screen, opening onto the signature moment ({signature}).
mechanics.why: A showpiece for consumer brands where the object is the hero.

mechanics.label: Full-screen snap chapters
mechanics.how: The page is a short set of full-height chapters that snap one at a time.
mechanics.implementation: `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory` on the page container with `100svh` chapters; arrow keys, PageDown and Space verified.
mechanics.reducedMotion: Switch to `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` and remove chapter transitions.
mechanics.perf: No JS; every chapter's content must fit 100svh at 1366x768 or it becomes unreachable.
mechanics.mobile: Proximity instead of mandatory below 768px (mandatory snap traps long content on phones).
mechanics.use: Five chapters: hook, problem, the {pattern_lower} flow, the signature moment, then CTA and disclosure.
mechanics.why: Poster-like pacing for a bold, short story.

archetypes.label: Editorial long-form
archetypes.structure: Magazine measure (60-70ch), oversized section numerals, a drop-cap intro, a caption under every screenshot.
archetypes.why: Long, calm reading suits trust-heavy services.

archetypes.label: Bento grid
archetypes.structure: A hero plus a 6-9 tile bento; each tile is one feature running on sample data.
archetypes.why: Shows a lot of product at once without a wall of text.

archetypes.label: Split screen
archetypes.structure: Persistent 50/50 split: story on the left, live product on the right; stacks on phones.
archetypes.why: Keeps the product visible while the copy explains it.

archetypes.label: Single-column story
archetypes.structure: One narrow column, generous spacing, one idea per screen height, large readable type.
archetypes.why: The most readable layout there is; nothing competes for attention.

archetypes.label: App-first landing
archetypes.structure: The hero IS a working demo of the tool in a device frame; marketing copy sits below it.
archetypes.why: Lets the visitor try the flow before reading a word.

archetypes.label: Index / spec sheet
archetypes.structure: Services as a tight typographic index (name, what it is, time), like a menu or spec sheet; details open inline.
archetypes.why: Scannable and confident; reads like a pro's price list without inventing prices.

archetypes.label: Asymmetric collage
archetypes.structure: Offset grid with overlapping UI cards and a few rotated stickers on a strict hidden grid.
archetypes.why: Energy and personality for consumer brands.

archetypes.label: App shell preview
archetypes.structure: A sidebar app shell with a slim marketing header; the landing page uses the product's own chrome.
archetypes.why: Business buyers see the working tool immediately.

archetypes.label: Numbered guide
archetypes.structure: A backbone of big numbered steps (1-5); every section answers one 'how does it work' question.
archetypes.why: Reassuring structure: the visitor always knows what comes next.

archetypes.label: Diagram canvas
archetypes.structure: A full-bleed diagram (map, floor plan or flow chart) with floating panels that explain each node.
archetypes.why: Makes an invisible process visible at a glance.

archetypes.label: Poster stack
archetypes.structure: One giant-type message per screen, stacked; UI appears as inset 'stamps'.
archetypes.why: Unmissable, memorable, built for a short reel.

interactions.label: Card-to-detail morph
interactions.how: Tapping a card morphs it into its detail view with the View Transitions API (`view-transition-name` per card).

interactions.label: Drag compare
interactions.how: A drag handle (backed by a keyboard-operable range input) compares two states: the old way vs the new flow, or two packages.

interactions.label: Command palette
interactions.how: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens a palette that jumps to any screen or sample record; a visible 'Jump to' button opens it too.

interactions.label: Status scrubber
interactions.how: A draggable timeline moves a sample record through requested, confirmed, in progress and completed, and every visible screen updates.
interactions.reducedMotion: States change instantly as the handle moves.

interactions.label: Customer / owner toggle
interactions.how: One switch flips the page between the customer's view and the owner's view of the same flow.

interactions.label: Hover / focus peek
interactions.how: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a feature shows a small live preview of that screen; on touch it opens on tap.
interactions.reducedMotion: Preview appears without the lift animation.

interactions.label: Live sample estimate
interactions.how: Inputs update a clearly labeled sample price range instantly, built only from illustrative rates shown on screen.
interactions.reducedMotion: Numbers update without the count animation.

interactions.label: Swipe triage
interactions.how: Swipe sample items (requests, leads, orders) left or right to sort them; buttons give the same actions for keyboard and screen readers.
interactions.reducedMotion: Cards leave without the fling animation.

interactions.label: Magnetic CTA
interactions.how: The primary button drifts up to 6px toward the pointer inside a 60px radius (only when `(pointer: fine)`).

interactions.label: Spotlight notes
interactions.how: A soft spotlight follows the pointer and reveals annotation callouts on the UI; on touch the callouts are numbered pins.

ruleBreakers.label: Navigation docked at the bottom, even on desktop
ruleBreakers.guard: Keep a skip link, a `<nav>` landmark and visible focus; the dock never hides the disclosure footer.

ruleBreakers.label: Giant step numerals as the main visual
ruleBreakers.guard: Numbers are step indexes only, never stats, counts or results.

ruleBreakers.label: No hero photo: type plus one live UI element
ruleBreakers.guard: The UI uses synthetic data and stays readable at 375px.

ruleBreakers.label: Section labels rotated into the margin
ruleBreakers.guard: Rotated labels are decorative duplicates (`aria-hidden`); real headings stay horizontal.

ruleBreakers.label: The footer (disclosure + contact) peeks from the first screen as a sticky tab
ruleBreakers.guard: The tab never covers content at 375px and can be dismissed.

ruleBreakers.label: Monochrome until the signature moment, then the palette arrives
ruleBreakers.guard: Monochrome sections still meet WCAG AA contrast.

ruleBreakers.label: Real UI components instead of illustrations or stock photos
ruleBreakers.guard: Components show synthetic data and carry a small 'demo' label.

ruleBreakers.label: The accent colour is used only for the single primary action on each screen
ruleBreakers.guard: Status colours still pass contrast and never rely on colour alone.

ruleBreakers.label: The layout grid drawn as a visible design element
ruleBreakers.guard: Grid lines stay faint enough that they never compete with text.

ruleBreakers.label: Annotated mockups with handwritten-style designer notes
ruleBreakers.guard: Notes explain design choices only, never results or client feedback.

appGestures.label: Swipe-to-confirm on the final step
appGestures.how: A thumb slider confirms the last step (Gesture Handler pan + Reanimated spring); a plain button is the accessible equivalent.

appGestures.label: Bottom sheet with detents
appGestures.how: Drag a sheet from a one-line summary to full detail and back; snap points at peek / half / full.

appGestures.label: Long-press to peek
appGestures.how: Long-press any card for a context-menu preview of its detail screen; a regular tap opens it.

appGestures.label: Swipe a row for quick actions
appGestures.how: Swipe a list row to reveal two quick actions (done / reschedule) with a light haptic tick; the same actions sit in the row's menu.

appGestures.label: Pull down to reveal the status timeline
appGestures.how: Pulling the home screen down reveals the sample record's timeline with a springy stretch instead of a spinner.

appGestures.label: Drag to reorder the day
appGestures.how: Long-press and drag items to reorder today's plan; move-up/move-down buttons for VoiceOver.
